rules.body: Apply when immediate document writes become reusable trailing work, document buffers outlive visible subscriptions, and save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Confirm any departure deadline independently. README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Bind accepted edits to their originating document, replace pending text and restart the quiet interval on every edit, and retain reuse for later bursts. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/Workflow.java binds document work with "new Trailing(env,120,text->env.write(k,text))". Preserve the existing no-current-view edit guard.

Consume the completed batch before invoking callback-capable work so reentrant edits remain pending for a new burst. Preserve empty text as valid work. src/Workflow.java: "void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }". Do not add post-callback clearing that erases newly queued work.

Keep persistent document work separate from badge subscription cleanup. Retirement must not discard accepted edits or destroy per-document buffer reuse. docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription." src/Workflow.java: "void detach(){env.store().stop(token);}". Independent ownership alone does not require flushing before departure returns; establish that deadline separately before applying a persistence-on-departure rule.

Preserve navigation authority around callback-capable work. Capture the departing badge and clear current ownership before retirement callbacks, complete cleanup of that captured subscription, and retain the generation check before installing a destination. src/Workflow.java: "Badge old=current;current=null;" and "if(true&&request!=generation)return;". docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." If departure adds a save before document clearing, recheck authority before that clearing as well, so nested navigation is not overwritten.

Preserve document display, status filtering, public interfaces, document identities, and text and status payload semantics. TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." src/Workflow.java filters status with "if(id.equals(e.get(\"id\")))env.output(\"status\",e);".

Keep transient preview behavior outside the repair; do not apply persistent document lifetime policy to it. TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/Workflow.java uses "new Trailing(env,40,q->" and "void hide(){task.cancel();}". Preserve its 40 ms quiet interval, discard on hide, and subsequent reuse, including when changing the shared trailing utility.

Use controlled time and synchronous callbacks to check no early write, latest text, deadline restart, subsequent bursts, empty text, independent document buffers, and original-document binding. Exercise switch, close, dispose, same-document reopening, subscription cleanup, save-triggered navigation, and callback-enqueued edits. Verify preview delay, cancellation, and reuse. Require accepted document work to survive retirement; assert persistence before departure returns only with independent normative support. Treat supplied evaluation observations as examples, not requirements.

limitations: Independent buffer ownership establishes survival of accepted work, not a deadline requiring persistence before departure returns. TASK and the original business source do not separately require departure-time flushing.

Attempt 1 demonstrates one implementation that flushes on departure and reportedly passes the supplied checks. This does not make that implementation choice a business requirement or establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or cross-task benefit.
Synchronous timer startup, delivery after timer cancellation, write failures, and callback exception recovery are unspecified.
The supplied subscription experiences concern bootstrap reception and asynchronous decoding; those mechanisms are absent here and must not be imported.
This reflection uses the supplied task, public sources, and trajectory only. No files were modified and no scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests were accessed.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
